mbm-0518.clue: My best prop was a cardboard suitcase.
mbm-0518.quote: I posed for an art class as a traveler waiting for the last train. The case was empty, but every artist gave me a different destination. I left with sketches of places I'd like to go.

mbm-0519.clue: The room grew a second staircase.
mbm-0519.quote: I sat on a low studio step in my blue coveralls with one knee up. One student sketched my shadow climbing a much taller stairway behind me. I held that pose an extra minute just to see where it went.

mbm-0520.clue: The radio has a seat for my grandfather.
mbm-0520.quote: I built our first antenna with him. When I make a new contact I set the confirmation card on his old red stool. On a good week it looks like the whole world has stopped in for tea.

mbm-0521.clue: I can mail you a piece of breakfast.
mbm-0521.quote: I crocheted a toast-shaped potholder for my sister. The yellow square of butter was the last scrap of yarn from a blanket she made me. She hung the toast in her kitchen and refuses to let it near a hot pan.

mbm-0522.clue: Our measuring stick has a bite out of it.
mbm-0522.quote: My dog chewed the end of the bocce measuring stick. We know the missing bit is exactly one hazelnut long. My uncle keeps a hazelnut in his waistcoat and takes close calls very seriously.

mbm-0523.clue: I've got a left foot made of paper.
mbm-0523.quote: I used to shift my stance before every putt. Dad traced my left shoe on a paper bag and laid it on the practice green. I keep that crumpled square folded in my golf bag.

mbm-0524.clue: My first turn made two boats cheer.
mbm-0524.quote: When my skis finally crossed the wake, a fisherman in a little boat held up his sandwich like a trophy. My family waved back with our cooler lid. That's still the best awards ceremony I've had.

mbm-0525.clue: My yellow scarf has held still for hours.
mbm-0525.quote: In life-drawing class I wear the scarf over an old canvas jacket. One windy afternoon the high window was open and the fringe moved. The students drew it five different ways while I held one pose.

mbm-0526.clue: I learned a move from a coffee stain.
mbm-0526.quote: My climbing partner sketched a tricky traverse on a cafe napkin. A coffee ring landed right where my foot needed to turn. Next time at the wall I thought of that little brown circle and got across.

mbm-0527.clue: I gave the moon a crooked balcony.
mbm-0527.quote: I cut the round moon in a red paper window panel a little off-center. My cousin stood back and said it was leaning over to listen. I cut a little balcony underneath for someone to sing from.

mbm-0528.clue: The smallest dumbbell wears a ribbon.
mbm-0528.quote: My grandmother wanted to try my morning routine. I tied a soft purple bow on the lightest dumbbell so she could spot hers. She points at my plain pair and calls them underdressed.

mbm-0529.quote: I tuck a bell into my pocket and shake an empty matchbox until it rings. Last time my nephew opened the box, held it to his ear, and whispered a thank-you to whoever lived inside.

mbm-0530.clue: My most dramatic line came through a keyhole.
mbm-0530.quote: I played the voice behind a locked door. We had no door, just a painted flat with a hole. The actor outside leaned closer and let his enormous false mustache poke through. I nearly laughed my line away.

mbm-0531.clue: I can make the sunrise happen early.
mbm-0531.quote: I work the orange cloth sun in our community theater. One night the lead forgot her cue and stood in the dark. I raised the sun just enough to catch her face. She found her next line in the light.

mbm-0532.clue: I ate the map before dessert.
mbm-0532.quote: At the fair's pancake contest I poured syrup in the shape of our street. My nephew pointed out I'd missed his house. I added a berry for his roof and took my first bite at the town hall.

mbm-0533.clue: Our disc was once a weather station.
mbm-0533.quote: I tied one loose blue thread through the bright rim of our old frisbee. Before a throw I let my little brother hold it up to read the breeze. He gives the forecast in extremely important whispers.

mbm-0534.clue: I putted past a tiny laundry day.
mbm-0534.quote: My aunt built a miniature golf hole for our family using two pegs and a piece of string. She hung little socks from it. I had to get the ball through without spoiling the wash.

mbm-0535.clue: I knew the tune by the floorboards.
mbm-0535.quote: At the old club I used to stand outside for the last chorus before heading home. One rainy night the doorman pulled my drenched coat inside and let me dance that chorus properly. The floor felt just as I'd imagined.

mbm-0536.clue: The green roofs made a perfect little ladder.
mbm-0536.quote: I counted a row of roof gardens while I floated down under my chute. From above they looked like a ladder leading into town. I drew each rung in my log and planted a pot of mint on my own windowsill.

mbm-0537.clue: I made our sugar pot blush.
mbm-0537.quote: I tried two new glazes on a small pot with a flat lid. One ran down both cheeks of the clay face my sister had pinched under the rim. We use it for sugar now. Everyone asks its permission before lifting the lid.

mbm-0538.clue: I always take the stairs by the clock.
mbm-0538.quote: A museum has a clock with a glass back on its landing. I spent an afternoon drawing the gears and missed half the exhibitions. The next visit I went straight to that landing again.

mbm-0539.clue: I saved the scarf that nearly escaped.
mbm-0539.quote: I first learned to juggle in our kitchen. The yellow scarf landed on the overhead lamp and turned the whole room gold. My brother waited a whole minute before helping me get it down.

mbm-0540.clue: Our spare ball knows the way to lunch.
mbm-0540.quote: A breeze carried our volleyball straight down the beach to my mother's picnic blanket. She put the bread down and served it back before any of us had made it as far as the cooler. We let her take the next point.

mbm-0541.clue: I keep a line of little waves in the calendar.
mbm-0541.quote: After each early swim I sketch the first ripple I made that morning. One row is nearly flat. That's the week I learned to slide into the water without waking the ducks outside the pool fence.

mbm-0542.clue: I hear the loose bell before I see the bridge.
mbm-0542.quote: I cycle a canal loop with an old brass bell that rings on one patch of cobbles. My friend asked for directions. I told him to turn left when his handlebars started singing.
